resources.string: Tap a console to see its setup steps: what is still needed before its games start, and what each step changes.
Ready to play, as far as Valkyr can see.
Steps left: %1$d
Emulator: %1$s is installed.
Emulator: %1$s is installed and runs this console with a core.
Emulator: none is installed for this console. Known ones: %1$s. Valkyr installs nothing; you install the app yourself.
Emulator: Valkyr knows no emulator for this console. It is no dead end: on a game page you can still choose any installed app to open the game with.
Core: RetroArch needs a core for this console (%1$s). In RetroArch: Load Core → Download a Core. Valkyr cannot see which cores RetroArch has; starting a game tells you.
BIOS: no BIOS folder is picked yet. This console asks for: %1$s.
BIOS: not found in your BIOS folder: %1$s.
BIOS: the required files are there. Optional and not found: %1$s.
BIOS: found (%1$s).
Saves: the folder of %1$s is set up in Save sync.
Saves: RetroArch’s saves or states folder is set up in Save sync.
Saves: no save folder is set up for this emulator, so its saves stay on this device. Not needed to play.
Discs: a game on several discs gets its .m3u list after the download.
Discs: automatic .m3u lists are switched off, so a game on several discs starts one disc at a time.
Changes nothing in Valkyr or your files.
You change this in RetroArch. The button opens RetroArch playlists, where you can set the core a playlist starts with; that is written into the playlist only after its own preview.
Opens the BIOS check. Only the BIOS folder setting changes; your files are only read.
Opens Save sync. Only the folder settings change; saves move when you start a sync.
Opens Settings. Only the automatic .m3u setting changes; a list is written beside a game after its download.
